title: Detection of Search Closed Sources
summary: This detection strategy covers the search of closed sources, the technique where an adversary buys or accesses material that is not public: criminal marketplaces, private forums, paid breach archives, closed messaging groups and commercial data brokers, in order to obtain credentials, employee records, source code or internal documents about the target. It matters because the purchase itself never touches the victim network, and the first visible effect is usually a credential being used or a document appearing in a negotiation, so the practical controls are external monitoring, insider risk signals and travel or expense anomalies for staff who buy data. The telemetry that makes it possible is brand and leak monitoring feeds, mail and messaging data loss prevention records, cloud egress logs for bulk downloads of sensitive repositories, endpoint detection records for archive creation, and expense or procurement review of unusual data broker payments. Detection fails because these services are designed to be unindexed and to resist monitoring, so most organisations only learn about the purchase after a leak is used.

beginner.definition: This detection looks for signs that someone bought private data about your company. Closed sources are places that search engines do not index, such as criminal markets and private forums. The rule watches leak feeds and large downloads of sensitive files. It also watches for staff who try to sell or share such data.
beginner.whyItMatters: A closed source may hold your passwords, contracts or customer lists. Buying that data is easier than breaking into your network. You cannot see the purchase, so you must watch the effect. Early warning lets you reset credentials before they are used.
howItWorks: External monitoring services watch criminal markets, paste sites and closed forums for your domains and product names.
Those services send matches to your security monitoring platform as structured alerts.
Inside the company, data loss prevention tools record when sensitive files are copied or uploaded.
Cloud audit logs record large downloads from code and document repositories by a single account.
The rule joins outside leak alerts with inside bulk access by the same business unit or time window.
Matches are reviewed with human resources and legal teams before any accusation is made.
beginner.example: Think of a hotel where a guest list was sold to a stranger. No door was forced and no camera recorded a break in. The first sign is a stranger greeting guests by name at the airport. This detection watches for that first greeting.
takeaways: Closed source purchases are invisible, so monitor the leak and the effect instead.
Join external leak alerts with internal bulk access before you judge a case.
Handle findings with legal and human resources teams, because a wrong accusation harms people.

objectives: Describe what closed sources are and why they are hard for defenders to see.
Identify the external monitoring and internal data access telemetry that supports this detection.
Write a correlation rule that joins leak alerts with bulk internal access.
Explain the legal and ethical steps required before acting on an insider finding.
Describe what response actions follow a confirmed credential or document leak.
dataSources: External brand and leak monitoring feeds that index criminal markets, paste sites and closed forums for company identifiers
Data loss prevention records for mail, messaging and removable media showing sensitive file movement
Cloud audit logs recording bulk downloads or exports from code repositories and document stores by one identity
Endpoint detection records for archive creation, encryption of document folders and staging of files before upload
Procurement and expense systems showing payments to data brokers or unusual research service vendors
logic: The pattern is an external leak alert that names company data, credentials or documents appearing shortly after an internal event in which one account or team accessed a far larger set of sensitive records than its normal baseline, especially when the access used a personal repository, an archive tool or an upload to an unsanctioned service. The fields that must be correlated are the external alert contents and source category, the downloading identity and its normal access baseline, the volume and classification of the files touched, the destination of any upload, and the time gap between the two events. The benign case is a legitimate migration, audit or legal hold in which a small team copies a large document set to an approved destination with a change record; the malicious case is a single account exporting a full repository or customer list to a personal account or removable media days before the same data appears in a closed source listing.
pseudoQuery:
# title: Sensitive Data Export Before External Leak Alert
# logsource:
#   product: azure
#   service: audit
# detection:
#   selection:
#     event_type|contains:
#       - 'FileDownloaded'
#       - 'RepositoryCloned'
#       - 'ArchiveCreated'
#     object_count: > 500
#   filter_approved:
#     destination|endswith:
#       - 'approved-migration-share'
#       - 'legal-hold-store'
#   condition: selection and not filter_approved
# level: high
falsePositives: A development team cloning a full repository during an approved platform migration with a change record
An audit or legal hold process that copies a large document set to an approved evidence store
A backup administrator running a one off full export after a storage system replacement
A sales operations analyst exporting a complete customer list for a board level reporting request
tuningNotes: Set the volume threshold per data classification rather than globally, because a code repository export and a customer list export have very different normal sizes, and require a change record or approved destination before the alert is sent to investigators. Baseline the largest export per account for ninety days and alert on new peaks that exceed it by a clear margin. Route findings to legal and insider risk reviewers rather than to the general queue, and record the case handling steps. Because most closed source activity never produces internal telemetry, keep the external monitoring feed running in parallel and accept that this rule only covers the subset of cases where the data left through your own estate.
